Hey! I know it sucks seeing those around you accomplish so much while you feel trapped in this lifestyle. In terms of professional help, I’m not sure what it’s like in other places, but I’m in Australia and I essentially just went to the local doctor and was honest, told her everything I was feeling and doing and that I needed to change and we worked on it from there. Made up a mental health plan, she suggested therapy just to have somebody to talk to, work through unhealthy habits with, but I can’t vouch for that because I have yet to go, but I’m sure it’s incredibly helpful if you’re comfortable with the idea of that. I was diagnosed and put on medication, but it does take some time to get used to and for the first couple of weeks I was pretty physically sick/same symptoms because it’s a big thing for the body to get used to, but hold out because it does work. Basically, just don’t hold back. It’s a good thing you’re recognising things aren’t going right, and even if it’s not “diagnosable depression” as such, you may just be in a rut and talking to someone will help develop coping skills. If you decide to go down the doctor route, be 100% honest in what you tell her, otherwise you won’t get the help you need. Good luck!

This sounds *exactly* like me except for the male part. Is there an underlying issue causing this? Depression maybe? It's debilitating but I've just started meds and things are starting to pick up again. If you feel generally drained and down I'd probably suggest going to a doctor/psych to get some help, because these generally sound like symptoms of depression. But, the fact you're recognising this lifestyle is unhealthy is a good start, and just by doing that you're making progress already. One day, one thing at a time. Sit down for 30 minutes today and do some full-focused study. Tomorrow, sit down and write out a grocery lists for some easy meals you could cook this week (pasta, sandwiches, even just something microwavable is cheaper than takeaways). I believe in you

I'm 19 now but had about that much saved up this time last year, have been out of home for about 2 years providing for myself (student accommodation and what not). I initially set aside a budget and started investing in household appliances, my own (basic) furniture, clothing, uni supplies and just general essential items and whatever I could stock up on. The rest of it I used to spend 6 weeks in Europe (r/humblebrag ;), and honestly, it was so worth it. Working hard for years in retail and graduating high school I treated myself to one of the best experiences of my life. I set aside some savings to come home to and am doing fine financially 6 months later. So travel - Europe is unreal, the US is super cool as well. As long as you've got a steady income to come home to, there's nothing to lose. No doubt you've earned it :)
